ageNotes: Healthy mix from late 30s upwards. Several active members in their early 40s.
lodgeCommunity: Welcomes members from all backgrounds. Strong tradition of friendship across professions and ages.
progressionPace: Standard — Master Mason 6 to 18 months after initiation
progressionNotes: We encourage new members to take on a progressive office shortly after they are raised but only if/when they feel ready to do so.
ritualQuality: Confident — ritual delivered reliably with occasional book use
ritualNotes: Emulation ritual performed to a good standard. Members encouraged but never pressured to learn parts.
regaliaRequired: Past Master / Master’s Apron (for those who have served as Worshipful Master)
Ritual book (purchased by candidate, not provided)
familyEventsOtherDetails: We often encourage wives and girlfriends to join us for a drink after a festive board.
interestOtherDetails: Many members are members or ex members of Upminster Hockey Club.  We are also proudly the only teetotal lodge in Essex, mainly out of respect for our forefathers.  Few in the lodge are actually teetotal and enjoy a social drink together before meetings, after the festive board, and at LOI.
whyJoin: Janus is a friendly, welcoming and progressive lodge.  We have been in existance over 100 years, and while we respect our history, we are focused on developing ourselves into a lodge for modern times.   Members regularly socialise outside of lodge meetings and LOI, with golf, theatre trips and curry nights being examples of the events we regularly hold either together or in smaller groups.  We look forward to welcoming you.
background:
Founded in 1922 in the aftermath of the Great War, Janus Lodge was established by men who understood that brotherhood, moral guidance, and mutual support were essential for rebuilding both communities and lives.

Named after the Roman god of transitions and new beginnings, our Lodge embraces the balance between honouring tradition and welcoming progress. This spirit runs through everything we do – from our ceremonies and charitable work to the time we spend together socially throughout the year.
traditionsNarrative: We are proud to be the only teetotal Lodge remaining in Essex – a unique tradition that honours our founding principles. That said, while no alcohol is served during Lodge meetings or formal dinners, our members do still enjoy a drink and good conversation outside the Lodge just as much as anyone else. It is part of what makes Janus distinctive: rooted in tradition, welcoming in spirit, and always good company.
charityNarrative:
Charity has always been central to the life of Janus Lodge. Every year, we raise funds for a range of good causes, combining Lodge collections with generous personal contributions from our members. While we support Masonic charities nationally, our priority is helping non-Masonic organisations that make a meaningful impact here in Essex.

Over the years, we have been proud to support charities that provide vital services – from comforting children in hospital to assisting families through hardship and backing essential community work.

You can explore some of the charities we support in the section alongside this text, where you will find links to learn more about the amazing work they do.

Being part of Janus Lodge means continuing a long tradition of generosity – and joining others who believe that brotherhood is about more than meetings; it is about making a difference.
memberExpectations: We are keen to maintain our hard-earned reputation for the high quality of work we do in meetings.  That's not to say that we expect perfection; we completely understand that not everyone enjoys or finds learning and performing ritual easy, all we ask is for you to do your best, and in return, you will receive support and encouragement to help you achieve what you want to achieve in your Masonic career.  We do ask all members to make every effort to attend all of our four meetings per year, along with LOI; not only those in office but also Past Masters whose experience and advice is invaluable to members progressing through the offices.
summary: A friendly, welcoming Lodge.  Traditional but very much forward-facing with a strong focus on close friendships and charity.   Suits candidates looking for genuine friendship, a committed and supportive lodge with a balanced approach to Masonic life.
